Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: In the RCT, vitamin C supplementation did not affect mood, including depression.
Sentence: "The vitamin C supplementation did not affect mood and serum concentrations of BDNF."
Measured as: depression (mood status)
Population: Healthy subjects with inadequate serum vitamin C (<50 μmol/L), n = 46
Intervention: Vitamin C 500 mg twice a day for 4 weeks
Comparator: Placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 260
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Patients with Scheuermann's disease and vitamin D deficiency had greater odds of depression than those without deficiency.
Sentence: "Patients with vitamin D deficiency had greater odds of pain (P < 0.0001), depression (P < 0.0001), suicide attempt (P = 0.0021), ED visits (P = 0.0246), and hospital admission (P < 0.0015)."
Measured as: depression
Population: Patients aged 0-18 years in the United States with Scheuermann's disease (TriNetX database)
Intervention: Vitamin D deficiency diagnosis (observational exposure)
Comparator: Patients with Scheuermann's disease without vitamin D deficiency diagnosis
Design: cohort study
Sample size: 11,277
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported
